- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model overreacts and forecasts continued rise; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or apply downward correction.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 0.5–1.5% downward bias for first 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or apply exponential decay to sentiment influence.  
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending downward; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to counteract mean reversion.
